title: Skybase pursues stablecoin distribution mainly through third-party venues rather than only its own app
content:
The Distribution Reward Primitive is `Active` for Skybase (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.1.1), and its Active Instances Directory lists eight live Instances (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.1.2.1–.2.8): the Sky.money App, Sky.money Open Source Widgets, DeFi Saver, CoW Swap, ParaSwap, Yearn (Gimme), MOM, and Lazy Summer Protocol.

Only two of the eight are Skybase's own surfaces. The rest are independent DeFi products with their own users, brands and frontends — several of them aggregators or venues that route users to whichever option is best, not to Sky specifically.

This puts real content behind Skybase's accessibility mandate. Rather than treating the Sky.money app as the funnel and everything else as competition, the Agent pays distribution rewards to whoever puts USDS in front of users. Reach is bought at the point where users already are, which is a materially different strategy from investing the same budget in its own interface.

The trade-off is dependency and commoditization. Demand generated through DeFi Saver or CoW Swap is demand Skybase does not own the relationship for, and it can be re-pointed at a competing stablecoin if the rewards stop. In exchange, Skybase gets distribution it could not build directly, and Sky.money's position is defended on product quality rather than on being the only door.

Notably the Sky.money app itself appears as an Instance of the *same* primitive on the same footing as external venues — the Agent's own channel is funded through the public, per-venue reward mechanism rather than through an unaccounted internal budget.
description: Eight Active Distribution Reward Instances cover DeFi Saver, CoW Swap, ParaSwap, Yearn (Gimme), MOM and Lazy Summer Protocol alongside the Sky.money app and its open-source widgets.
